dedupe_keys.name: seattle building energy benchmarking data 2015 present

description: Seattle's Building Energy Benchmarking Program (SMC 22.920) requires owners of non-residential and multifamily buildings larger than 20,000 square feet to track energy performance and report it to the city each year, and under Ordinance 125000 the city publishes the data for all such buildings. The dataset holds benchmarking records for reporting years 2015 to 2024 with 46 fields: building identifiers, name, type, tax parcel, address, coordinates, neighbourhood, year built, floors, gross floor areas, ENERGY STAR score, site and source energy use intensity (weather normalised and not), electricity, steam and natural gas use, property use types, compliance status and issues, and total greenhouse gas emissions and intensity. Coverage: covered buildings in Seattle. Access: CSV, JSON and Socrata API from Seattle Open Data, with a companion table of performance ranges by building type. Licence: public domain; free. Caveats: values are reported through ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and include non-compliant or flagged records. Simulation uses are energy baselines and calibration targets for city building stock models and emissions performance standards. Related records: NYC Local Law 84 benchmarking.
